facts.statement: Psammodus lived during the Late Devonian to the Early Carboniferous periods.
facts.quote: Psammodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish known from the Late Devonian to the Early Carboniferous period.

facts.statement: Psammodus were carnivores that ate hard-shelled prey.
The genus Psammodus was first described and named by the naturalist Louis Agassiz.
facts.quote: Fossils of the genus Psammodus were first described and named by naturalist Louis Agassiz.

facts.statement: Psammodus is the only known member of the family Psammodontidae and the order Psammodontiformes.
facts.quote: It is the only member of the family Psammodontidae and the order Psammodontiformes

facts.statement: Psammodus serves as the type genus for both the family Psammodontidae and the order Psammodontiformes.
facts.quote: Psammodus is the type genus of the family Psammodontidae and the order Psammodontiformes.

facts.statement: Fossils of Psammodus are primarily known from their plate-like teeth.
facts.quote: Psammodus are known primarily from their plate-like teeth.

facts.statement: The teeth of Psammodus were broad, flat, and often rectangular or triangular in shape.
facts.quote: These teeth are broad and flat, and often appear rectangular or triangular.

facts.statement: In life, the teeth of Psammodus were tightly packed together within the jaws.
facts.quote: In life the teeth were tightly packed together in the jaws.

facts.statement: The tooth plates of Psammodus were specifically adapted for durophagy.
facts.quote: Psammodus tooth plates are adapted for durophagy

facts.statement: Psammodus likely ate small benthic invertebrates with hard shells and occasionally small fish, similar to modern chimaeras.
facts.quote: members of the genus likely had similar diets to living chimaeras consisting of small benthic invertebrates with hard shells and occasional small fish.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Psammodus ground food between its upper and lower tooth plates instead of crushing it.
facts.quote: Food was likely ground between the upper and lower tooth plates, rather than being crushed.

facts.statement: The time range for Psammodus is recorded from the Tournaisian to the Bathonian, between 358.86 and 165.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tournaisian to Bathonian (358.86 to 165.3 million years ago)
